risk_factors.risk: Authoring pipeline produces DL-013 boilerplate despite quality gate rules
risk_factors.mitigation: Governance guard Rule 2 and Rule 6 active from first write. Pre-commit hook: scan for 'represents a plausible misconception' and 'A candidate may select this option by misapplying' — block commit if detected. Per-item authoring checklist includes boilerplate scan.

risk_factors.risk: Difficulty labels inflated (DL-031 pattern) — definition-match items labeled Moderate when Easy
risk_factors.mitigation: Per-item justification required for any item labeled Moderate or above. Rule: if stem-CorrectChoice lexical overlap > 50%, default difficulty is Easy unless distractors require genuine Application-level discernment. Quality gate audit includes random-sample difficulty calibration check.

risk_factors.risk: Dual-block architecture accidentally introduced in late packs
risk_factors.mitigation: Pre-commit validation: every item must be a single JSON object (no paired-object pattern). scan_dualblock_p2.js runs on each pack before quality gate. Single-object is enforced by template — authoring tools emit single objects only.

risk_factors.risk: Pack E cross-domain items accidentally test Part 1 concepts (e.g., cost allocation instead of corporate finance + ethics)
risk_factors.mitigation: Cross-domain items tagged with explicit SectionTags array ['F','B'] etc. Cross-part boundary validator (Rule 10) flags P1- terminology. Domain validator rejects Section A/C/D/E/F from Part 1's topic registry.

risk_factors.risk: Authoring throughput falls below target (500 items per 2 weeks = 36 items/day)
risk_factors.mitigation: Monitor item count daily during each pack window. If behind by >15% at midpoint (e.g., <250 items by end of Week 3 for Pack A), escalate for additional authoring resources. Accept <500 items if quality is maintained (minimum 475 per pack, deficit addressed in Phase 3).

risk_factors.risk: Numeric answer-key errors (DL-030) in calculation-heavy packs (C, B, E)
risk_factors.mitigation: Every numeric item must be independently recalculated by a second agent before quality gate. Pack C (highest calculation density) requires 100% double-verification. Pack B WACC/CAPM items require formula-substitution trace in explanation.

risk_factors.risk: Certification throughput insufficient — 2,500 items at 60/hr = 42 hours of processing
risk_factors.mitigation: Batch-process via multiple parallel certification agents. Pack A and Pack C can certify in parallel (different files). Governance guard Rule 5 (≤30 items/batch) governs batch size but not parallelism. Target: 3 parallel certification streams × 60 items/hr = 180 items/hr → 14 hours total.

risk_factors.risk: High number of items fail certification (LOW confidence on ≥2 dimensions)
risk_factors.mitigation: If >10% of items (250) fail certification, escalate to architecture review. Root cause likely in authoring pipeline or formula errors. Stop certification and re-audit affected packs before resuming. Editorial Queue items tracked with remediation plans.

risk_factors.risk: Case authoring introduces DL-023 pattern (Body instead of Headers+Rows on table exhibits)
risk_factors.mitigation: Case exhibit validator checks for Headers + Rows presence on all Type: 'table' exhibits. Pre-commit hook blocks Body-only exhibits. Template enforcement: case authoring tool emits Headers + Rows, never Body.

risk_factors.risk: Case cognitive progression not enforced — items at wrong Bloom's levels for their position
risk_factors.mitigation: Progression validator checks each case: items 1-2 must be Apply (calculation), items 3-4 must be Analyze (interpretation), item 5 must be Evaluate (judgment). Flag any case that deviates for human review.

risk_factors.risk: Blueprint coverage gaps discovered late — some LOS underserved
risk_factors.mitigation: Run preliminary coverage scan at M3.2 (50% certified — 1,250 items). By midpoint, coverage pattern should be visible. Adjust remaining certification/authoring to fill gaps. Late discovery (Week 15) may require extension into Phase 4.

risk_factors.risk: Difficulty audit reveals systematic DL-031 inflation across multiple packs
risk_factors.mitigation: Run difficulty calibration sample audit during Phase 2 quality gates (not deferred to Phase 3). Catch inflation early. Per-item justification requirement during authoring prevents most DL-031 occurrences. Audit at M3.8 is confirmatory, not corrective.

risk_factors.risk: End-to-end simulation reveals rendering bugs in app.js for Part 2 content
risk_factors.mitigation: app.js has been tested incrementally: skeleton (Phase 1), 2,500 MCQs (Phase 2), cases (Phase 3). By Phase 4, most rendering paths are exercised. Focus simulation on edge cases: cross-domain items with dual SectionTags, match-type questions, multi-select scoring. Any bug found at this stage is isolated — fix does not require re-certification.

risk_factors.risk: Cross-part collision audit discovers Part 1 concepts in Part 2 items — requires content fixes
risk_factors.mitigation: Part 2 uses single-object architecture — fixes are mechanical (edit offending item, no dual-block coordination). Affected items move from Certified → Editorial Queue. Fixes must be re-verified before release. Budget 1 week buffer for this scenario.

risk_factors.risk: Performance benchmarks fail — pack parsing or rendering exceeds targets
risk_factors.mitigation: Part 2 packs are same size as Part 1 (500 items each). Part 1 app.js already handles 500-item packs. Performance should be comparable. If parsing is slow, investigate string-aware brace-matcher efficiency. Defer non-critical optimizations to post-release.

risk_factors.risk: Governance guard final sweep finds violations that were missed in Phase 3 certification
risk_factors.mitigation: Governance guard has been active since Phase 1 — violations should be near-zero by Phase 4. Any discovery indicates a guard rule gap or scan methodology error. Treat as governance incident: investigate root cause, fix guard if needed, remediate items, re-certify.

risk_factors.risk: Repository freeze finds root directory hygiene violations (temp files, reports, scripts in root)
risk_factors.mitigation: Root hygiene has been enforced since Phase 1. Automated check runs at each milestone. If violations found at freeze, they are likely new files written during Phase 4 testing. Cleanup is mechanical and non-destructive.

risk_factors.risk: Schedule slip — Phase 3 takes longer than 5 weeks, compressing Phase 4
risk_factors.mitigation: Phase 4's minimum viable scope: end-to-end simulation (M4.1), governance sweep (M4.3), release (M4.5). M4.2 (collision audit) and M4.4 (performance) can be parallelized. M4.6 (documentation) can extend past Week 18 if needed — does not block release.

critical_path: Phase 1 must complete before Phase 2 starts because: governance guard must be active to enforce single-object architecture and prevent DL-008/DL-013/DL-026 from first write; FORMULA_MASTER_P2.md must exist for formula reference during question authoring; app.js must load skeleton files to validate authoring format; validation scripts must pass on empty skeletons to establish error baseline.

Pack A must complete and pass Quality Gate A before Pack C starts because: sequential authoring prevents defect patterns from propagating across packs; quality gate findings inform improvements to authoring process for subsequent packs; Pack A establishes the single-object template that all subsequent packs follow.

Pack C must complete and pass Quality Gate C before Pack B starts because: Pack C has highest calculation intensity (55% numeric/calculation items) — any arithmetic error patterns discovered must be corrected before authoring Pack B's WACC/CAPM items; Pack C's quality gate findings inform formula-verification process for remaining packs.

Pack B must complete and pass Quality Gate B before Pack D starts because: Pack B introduces corporate finance formulas (CAPM, WACC, EOQ, CCC) that share risk-return concepts with Pack D's Domain E (NPV, IRR); Pack B's formula-verification lessons apply to Pack D.

Pack D must complete and pass Quality Gate D before Pack E starts because: Pack D is the only dual-domain pack — experience managing domain boundaries informs Pack E's cross-domain items (375 Domain F + 125 Cross-domain); Pack E's cross-domain items require mature domain-boundary enforcement.

Phase 2 must complete before Phase 3 starts because: all 2,500 items must be authored and structurally validated before certification begins; certification pipeline processes items in batches across all packs — incomplete packs would require pipeline restart; answer-key verification requires complete pack for cross-reference.

Phase 3 must complete before Phase 4 starts because: end-to-end simulation requires certified items (non-certified items excluded from learner pool per governance rules); cross-part collision audit requires complete content pool; blueprint coverage analysis must inform final delivery validation.
